sources.entry: connexion - A spec-first framework that handles requests based on your OpenAPI specification.

summary.one_liner: Connexion is a spec-first Python web framework that routes, validates, and serializes requests based on your OpenAPI (or Swagger) specification.
summary.what_it_does: Connexion takes an OpenAPI or Swagger specification and automatically registers routes, linking each operation to a Python function via its operationId. It validates request headers, parameters, and bodies and response bodies against the spec, and unpacks parameters into function arguments. It serializes returned Python objects into responses and handles authentication separately from application logic. It can run as a standalone app via AsyncApp or FlaskApp, or wrap an existing ASGI or WSGI app through ConnexionMiddleware. A Swagger UI console and a command line tool (connexion run) for testing and mocking a spec are also provided.
use_cases: Build a REST API from an OpenAPI spec
Validate incoming requests against an API specification
Serve interactive API documentation with Swagger UI
Mock or test an OpenAPI spec from the command line
Add OpenAPI-driven routing to an existing ASGI or WSGI app
Migrate a Flask-based API from Connexion 2.x
how_to_run: app.run()  # development only, requires uvicorn extra
uvicorn run:app  # production, with an ASGI server
notable: Spec-first: the OpenAPI document drives routing, validation, and serialization instead of generating the spec from code
Automatic route registration via operationId, with no route decorators needed
Can run standalone or wrap any ASGI or WSGI framework
Optional extras for Swagger UI, uvicorn, and Flask support
Built-in connexion run CLI to test and mock a specification
caveats: Requires writing a detailed OpenAPI spec first, so the spec must be kept in sync with code
app.run() is recommended only for development; production needs an external ASGI server
Swagger UI and uvicorn features need optional extras installed
